input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 8.1 sets a three-year term, and the termination rights in Section 9 are limited to material breach (9.1), insolvency (9.2) and Vendor security/service/legal/IP failures (9.3); Sections 6.2, 19.4 and 27.3 are cause-based remedies only. No convenience right exists for either Party, and Section 2.1 expressly negates Customer termination rights in a take-or-pay multi-year commitment, which is walk-away territory under the rule. We insert a new Section 9.4 giving Customer a 30-day convenience exit with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term, and conform Section 2.1 (retaining its reduction restriction) so it does not contradict the new right. Vendor's non-renewal/renewal mechanics in Section 8.2 are not affected.

proposal.summary: Add Customer convenience termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund; confirm Vendor has no convenience right; conform Section 2.1
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a Customer-only convenience exit on thirty days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and confirmed Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term, as our playbook requires in a three-year commitment. We also conformed Section 2.1 so its take-or-pay language no longer negates that exit, while leaving the reduction restriction intact.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, on thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees pro rata for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

ops.oldText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction rights and without termination rights other than as expressly provided in Section 9.4.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
